settings.routing.httpDownstream.label: HTTP client routing
settings.routing.httpDownstream.descript: Choose how browser and SSE callers use persistent upstream sessions.
settings.routing.strategy.label: Routing strategy
settings.routing.strategy.description: Choose how requests are distributed across accounts.
settings.routing.strategy.guide.capacity: Good default for compliant mixed-account pools; prefers accounts with more usable quota headroom.
settings.routing.strategy.guide.relative: Similar to capacity weighted, but smooths selection through a weighted draw over the strongest available accounts.
settings.routing.strategy.guide.usageWei: Spreads traffic by observed usage and can react to recent consumption patterns.
settings.routing.strategy.guide.roundRob: Cycles evenly through eligible accounts without considering quota shape.
settings.routing.strategy.guide.fillFirs: Uses one account heavily before moving on; useful for controlled drain tests, but less conservative for normal traffic.
settings.routing.strategy.guide.sequenti: Drains accounts in a fixed order. Prefer for maintenance windows, not everyday blended usage.
settings.routing.strategy.guide.resetDra: Prioritizes accounts around quota reset timing so expiring capacity is consumed first.
settings.routing.strategy.guide.singleAc: Pins all routed traffic to one selected active account.
settings.routing.strategy.safetyNote: No strategy can guarantee account-safety outcomes. For low-volume policy-compliant use, prefer capacity weighted or relative availability with sticky threads enabled so traffic stays steady and session-local.
settings.routing.stickyThreads.label: Sticky threads
settings.routing.stickyThreads.descripti: Keep normal requests for the same session on the same account when possible. This is a soft preference, not a guarantee.
settings.routing.stickyThreads.hardAffin: Turning this off does not disable hard Codex continuation affinity: a request that carries Codex continuation state (turn state, a previous response, or uploaded files) may still require its original owner account unless codex-lb can safely migrate or replay it.
settings.routing.preferEarlier.label: Prefer earlier reset
settings.routing.preferEarlier.descripti: When several accounts are otherwise eligible, prefer those whose selected quota window resets sooner. Weekly resets are compared by day. Applies to the capacity weighted, usage weighted, and fill first strategies.
settings.routing.promptCacheTtl.label: Prompt-cache affinity TTL
settings.routing.promptCacheTtl.descript: Keep OpenAI-style prompt-cache mappings warm for a bounded number of seconds.
settings.routing.warmupModel.label: Warmup model
settings.routing.warmupModel.description: Set the model used by the normal warmup endpoint.
settings.routing.additionalQuota.title: Additional quota routing policies
settings.routing.additionalQuota.descrip: Override account routing for model-specific quota pools.
settings.routing.relativeAvailability.po: Raise normalized relative-availability scores to this power before weighted selection.
settings.routing.relativeAvailability.to: Keep only the strongest weighted candidates before the final random draw.
settings.routing.overload.title: Routing weights and overload isolation
settings.routing.overload.description: Tune how in-flight work and recent failures shift traffic between accounts, and how long a repeatedly overloaded account is held out. Leave a field empty to inherit the environment value or default.
settings.routing.overload.isolationSecon: After the third overload trip, hold the account out of fresh selection and reroute soft sticky sessions for this long. 0 keeps the short soft backoff only.
settings.routing.overload.inflightPenalt: Usage percent added per in-flight request so busy accounts look fuller to weighted routing (0-100).
settings.routing.overload.leaseTokenWeig: Multiplier applied to a turn's reserved tokens before they count as usage pressure.
settings.routing.overload.leaseTtlSecond: A per-account lease older than this is reclaimed as stale; long streams stay covered by their request budget plus a grace period. Must be at least the proxy and compact request budgets.
settings.routing.overload.errorRateWeigh: Weight selection by recent error rate
Capacity-weighted and relative-availability strategies draw a flaky account less often once ten outcomes are in its ten-minute window.
settings.routing.singleAccount.label: Selected account
settings.routing.singleAccount.descripti: Route every eligible request through one account until this setting changes.
settings.routing.singleAccount.empty: Import an account before enabling single-account routing.
settings.routing.subscriptionOverflow.la: Overflow to model source when all subscription accounts are exhausted
settings.routing.subscriptionOverflow.de: When every eligible subscription account has hit its usage limit, new requests are sent to this source at its own cost. Default off. Turning it off stops new overflow immediately; conversations already pinned to the source keep working until their pins expire.
settings.routing.subscriptionOverflow.lo: Model sources could not be loaded; overflow cannot be configured until they load.

settings.routing.subscriptionOverflow.he: Triggers only on pool-wide usage exhaustion (the same condition that returns 429 usage_limit_reached with resets_at) — never on local caps, fair-share throttles, transient errors, auth failures or a single account's rate limit.

Eligible: new conversations or requests without prior reasoning on standard Responses models, unscoped API keys only. gpt-5.6 conversations cannot overflow in this version. Declare the tool types your source supports (custom, apply_patch, web_search, shell, tool_search) on its model entries. Background jobs never overflow.

A conversation that received source output stays on the source (7-day idle limit; compaction is unavailable there). Disabling or deleting the source ends reasoning-bearing conversations with an error and returns the others to subscription accounts.

Limited API keys stream live and are charged an estimate when the source omits usage or the client disconnects mid-answer. Fast mode is served at standard tier. Source rate limits show in Codex as "exceeded retry limit, last status: 429".

/status shows the subscription pool. A Codex session downgraded to HTTP stays on HTTP until restart. While overflow is on, routing depends on the proxy database. Forked conversations may replay reasoning the source cannot read.

cacheProbe.title: Cross-account cache isolation probe
cacheProbe.description: Send one single-use 28k-token prefix on a seed account, then the identical bytes on its siblings, and read back how much each one was served from cache.
cacheProbe.cost.summary: Estimated cost: {{calls}} calls, about {{tokens}} input tokens of real quota.
cacheProbe.cost.noAccounts: No eligible accounts: the probe needs a seed plus at least one other active account.
cacheProbe.pressure.generic: The account pool is under pressure; the probe will not spend quota right now.
cacheProbe.confirm.title: Run the cache isolation probe?
cacheProbe.confirm.description: This sends {{calls}} real requests and spends about {{tokens}} input tokens of account quota. It cannot be undone.
cacheProbe.interpretation.seedMisses: How to read this: a hit on a non-seed account means the upstream prefix cache is not partitioned per account. Hits are sporadic for every caller, so a miss on the seed account is expected and is not a failure of the probe — and a run with no cross-account hit is evidence, not proof.
cacheProbe.result.counts: {{otherHits}}/{{otherCalls}} other accounts hit · {{seedHits}}/{{seedCalls}} seed repeats hit
cacheProbe.verdicts.cross_account_sharin: A non-seed account read back content only the seed had ever sent, so the upstream prefix cache is not partitioned per account.
cacheProbe.verdicts.no_cross_account_hit: The seed cached but no sibling did. That is evidence of isolation, not proof: hits are sporadic, so repeat the run before concluding.
cacheProbe.verdicts.inconclusive.label: Inconclusive
cacheProbe.verdicts.inconclusive.detail: Nothing cached on the seed either, or every sibling call failed, so this run cannot tell isolation apart from an ordinary cache miss. Run it again.
cacheProbe.toasts.crossAccountHit: Cross-account cache hit: the upstream prefix cache is not partitioned per account.
